hypotheses.reasoning: Starting at 22:00:46, catalog-svc's PutObject calls to S3 in us-east-1 began failing fast with errors from AWS itself: first 503 ServiceUnavailable (#124, #129), then 500 InternalError (#140, #147). Before that, catalog-svc was healthy, with batch calls finishing in 30–85ms. Because of the failed S3 writes, catalog-svc returned 500 'storage write failed' to search-api (#127, #136), and web-bff then returned 500s on GET /search. The 500s at web-bff (#126 onward), the exhausted AWS SDK retry quota (#133) and the slow edge latencies are spread symptoms, not the cause. Errors stopped after about 22:05, when catalog-svc calls succeeded again (#161). I found no deploy, and catalog-db and redis-cache showed no errors. The first 503s say 'reduce your request rate', which could mean S3 throttling us rather than an AWS fault. But the later 500 InternalErrors point to a problem on AWS's side.
The 'reduce your request rate' throttling plus 52 retries in 60s could be our own retries making S3 throttling worse.
One malformed catalog.updates message was moved to the dead-letter queue at 21:55. That was handled correctly and nothing jammed, so it's most likely unrelated.

verdict.recommendedAction: Check the AWS Health Dashboard for an S3 problem in us-east-1 and open an AWS support case with the request IDs (3D87FDE, AFF5E99). Make search reads stop depending on artifact writes: run the S3 PutObject asynchronously or best-effort with backoff, so a failed write doesn't fail GET /search. Consider failing over to a replica bucket in another region.
